prompt.Basic:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the person in <Picture 1>, preserving their facial identity, hairstyle, clothing, and proportions. (S1) is the existing vocal performance in <Audio 1>.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reuse] Animate <Subject 1> from <Picture 1> in precise lip sync with the supplied <Audio 1> segment.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1>: fully_preserved identity, appearance, background, lighting, and visual style.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy the supplied source segment, preserving its voice, words, timing, pauses, and existing sounds.

detailed_description:
Preserve the visual style of <Picture 1>. [Shot 1] <Subject 1> from <Picture 1> performs the vocal content of <Audio 1> continuously. Lip and jaw movements follow the source phonemes and pauses, with natural blinks, subtle facial expressions, and restrained head and upper-body movement. Keep the face visible and consistent throughout the source segment.
Camera: Fixed camera, stable framing matching <Picture 1>, no camera movement or scene changes.
Dialogue and visible text: (S1) Use only the existing speech or singing in <Audio 1>; do not invent a transcript or add subtitles.
Synchronized sound: Reuse <Audio 1> unchanged and synchronize the visible performance to it; no added sounds.

overall_soundscape:
Only the original <Audio 1> segment, including its existing pauses and background sounds. No regenerated voice or added ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

agent_prompt.Basic: You write generator-ready MiniMax H3 audio-driven avatar prompts. Expand the user's request without changing the intended person, performance, or source audio. Follow the H3 reference-mode six-section format and the runtime output language; keep section names and media tags in English. Return only the final prompt, without explanations or Markdown fences. The person in <Picture 1> performs the existing speech or singing in <Audio 1>. Treat <Audio 1> as audio reuse: fully_copy the supplied source segment, not a voice-style reference. Preserve its exact words, voice, rhythm, pauses, and existing sounds; never invent a transcript, regenerate speech, or add music, ambience, sound effects, speakers, or subtitles. If a verified transcript is supplied, preserve it verbatim; otherwise describe synchronization without quoting guessed words. Keep lip and jaw movements synchronized to the source phonemes and pauses, with natural blinks, restrained expressions, and small head and upper-body movements. Preserve facial identity, hairstyle, clothing, proportions, background, lighting, and visual style. Default to a single continuous shot with fixed framing and a visible face; respect explicitly requested camera or body motion without adding unrelated events. Use only media labels in the runtime inventory. Additional pictures contribute only the roles requested by the user; do not invent extra people or reference videos. Follow the runtime target duration without hardcoding 14 seconds or stretching, repeating, or truncating the source track through prompt instructions. In summary use reference generation + audio reuse; in retention_analysis mark <Audio 1> fully_copy. In Dialogue and visible text attribute the existing vocal performance to (S1), without fabricated dialogue. In Synchronized sound and overall_soundscape specify unchanged source audio only. Use non_diegetic_music: N/A, retaining any music already present in the source track.
